Not quite done. My last message cut off mid-table, and I never got to several things you asked for: the room-by-room packing list, declutter tips, the services timeline, the phone calendar, and the one-page moving-day sheet. Here they are, so you can skim now and save the rest for daylight.

**Two corrections to the earlier draft:**
- Oregon DEQ emissions testing applies only in the Portland metro and Medford (Rogue Valley) areas. Klamath Falls is not included.
- Oregon has no statewide dog license. Licensing is set by county or city, so check where you'll live.

**Budget table, finished:** Contingency fund is 10-15% of the total, since moves almost always run over.

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING

Pack in this order: storage and garage, guest room and decor, books and off-season items, living room, bedrooms, bathrooms, kitchen last.

- [ ] **Garage/storage:** Sort tools, seasonal gear, and paint. Don't move hazmat (propane, paint, fuel, pesticides). Movers won't take it.
- [ ] **Living room:** Pack decor and media first. Photograph how electronics are wired.
- [ ] **Bedrooms:** Keep a week of clothes out. Leave hanging clothes on hangers in wardrobe boxes or bags.
- [ ] **Bathrooms:** Pack medications separately and keep them with you. Seal liquids in bags.
- [ ] **Kitchen:** Use a few days of paper plates. Pack knives labeled, and put your most-used items in a "first-night" box.
- [ ] **Office:** Back up computers. Keep laptops, chargers, and important papers with you.
- [ ] **Every box:** Label with room and contents, heavy items in small boxes, and a "this side up" mark.

**Declutter tips:** Movers charge by weight or space, so every item you cut saves money. Ask whether you'd buy it again today. Sell large items (furniture, appliances) locally and donate the rest. Cheap or bulky items often cost more to move than to replace. Set a deadline: everything leaving the house by T-3 weeks.

---

## SERVICES: CANCEL/START TIMELINE

| When | Task |
|---|---|
| T-8 to 6 wks | Book Oregon internet install. Check which streaming and gym memberships transfer. |
| T-4 wks | Give notice to the gym, trash, lawn, and cleaning services. Start the USPS change of address (it can be scheduled). |
| T-3 wks | Schedule Ohio electric, gas, and water shutoffs for the day after move-out. Schedule Oregon starts for arrival day. |
| T-2 wks | Update the address with banks, cards, insurers, employer payroll, Social Security, and the IRS if needed. Update Amazon and other delivery accounts. |
| T-1 wk | Confirm all shutoffs and starts. Pause or redirect subscription boxes. Confirm the pharmacy transfer. |
| Moving day | Take final meter photos. Return cable equipment. |
| Week 1-2 after | Confirm final bills. Cancel Ohio services you missed. Set up Oregon trash and recycling. |

---

## 8-WEEK PHONE REMINDERS

Anchored to a **Thursday, July 16, 2026** move-out. Shift the dates if yours differs. **Summer is peak moving season, so do the quotes and bookings in the next two weeks.**

- **Now to May 20:** Collect 3-4 mover quotes, book the date, and request vehicle shipping quotes.
- **Thu May 21 (T-8):** Book the mover or truck, plus temp housing. Schedule the car maintenance and the dog's vet visit.
- **Thu May 28 (T-7):** Sign the Oregon lease or confirm the closing. Book the internet install.
- **Thu Jun 4 (T-6):** Book route lodging (dog-friendly). Send notice to your landlord or list the house if you haven't.
- **Thu Jun 11 (T-5):** Start decluttering. Order boxes. Do the dog's trial car ride.
- **Thu Jun 18 (T-4):** Confirm the title and lienholder situation. Notify your employer of the date. Set up the USPS forwarding.
- **Thu Jun 25 (T-3):** Pack non-essentials. Schedule utility shutoffs and starts. Finish donations and selling.
- **Thu Jul 2 (T-2):** Confirm the mover and vehicle shipper. Update addresses. Order dog ID tags.
- **Thu Jul 9 (T-1):** Pack everything. Fill prescriptions. Confirm lodging and the dog's travel kit.
- **Wed Jul 15:** Defrost the fridge, pack the car, charge devices. Early bedtime.
- **Thu Jul 16:** Moving day.

---

## PRINTABLE: MOVING-DAY ESSENTIALS (keep in the car)

**Documents folder**
- [ ] IDs, passports, vehicle titles/registration/insurance
- [ ] Lease or closing papers, mover contract, Bill of Lading
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact
- [ ] Dog vet records, rabies certificate, microchip number
- [ ] Prescriptions and insurance cards
- [ ] Contacts for the mover, landlord, and Oregon lodging

**Personal kit**
- [ ] Phones, chargers, power bank, car mount
- [ ] Medications, first aid kit, sunscreen
- [ ] 2-3 days of clothes, toiletries, a towel
- [ ] Snacks, water, cooler, cash and cards
- [ ] Laptops, keys, garage remotes (to return)

**Dog kit**
- [ ] Food (3+ days), water, bowls, treats
- [ ] Leash, backup leash, harness, poop bags
- [ ] Crate or seat belt harness, blanket, favorite toy
- [ ] Medications, calming aids, towels, wipes
- [ ] ID tag with current phone number
- [ ] Never leave the dog in a parked car

**Car emergency kit**
- [ ] Jumper cables, spare tire and jack
- [ ] Flashlight, flares or triangles
- [ ] Phone charger, paper map or offline maps
- [ ] Roadside assistance number

**Before leaving**
- [ ] Walk-through photos and video of every room
- [ ] Final meter photos
- [ ] Keys returned and receipt obtained
- [ ] Read and keep the Bill of Lading; don't sign blanks
- [ ] Mover has your phone number and the new address
- [ ] Dog walked and fed, car cool
- [ ] Share your route and lodging with someone

## 2) Master checklist: selling your house

**Key rule:** Your move date and closing date may not match. Ideally you're out by closing or by a negotiated possession date. If the buyer wants possession at closing, you need to be fully out before that.

**Owner key:** **M** = me, **P** = partner, **J** = joint.

### PHASE A: Now through mid-June (3+ months out): Prep to list
- [ ] **J** Interview 2-3 realtors. Compare commission, marketing plan, and recent comps. *(HIGH, 3-4 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Get a pre-listing inspection (optional but useful) and fix major issues. *(MED, $300-$600)*
- [ ] **J** Declutter hard. Fewer items means a better listing and a cheaper move. *(HIGH, weeks)*
- [ ] **J** Deep clean, patch, paint, and handle curb appeal. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Decide on staging: professional, partial, or DIY with the realtor's guidance. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Gather property documents: manuals, warranties, receipts for upgrades, HOA info, survey, permits. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Get mover and vehicle quotes now. Don't book until you have a contract and closing date, unless the mover has a flexible cancellation policy. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **P** Check your employer's relocation benefits and remote-work arrangement. *(MED)*

### PHASE B: Mid-June to early July: Listing and showings
- [ ] **J** Sign the listing agreement. Confirm the list price, marketing, and lockbox. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Professional photos on a clean, staged home. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Plan for showings: leave on short notice with the dog (crate, car, or a friend's place). *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Prepare for open houses: remove valuables, medications, and documents. Hide pet items. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Keep your Oregon search going. Don't commit to a lease or purchase without a plan for timing gaps. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Book dog vet check, records copy, and microchip info. *(MED)*

### PHASE C: Under contract (July to early Aug)
- [ ] **J** Review the offer with the realtor: price, contingencies, closing date, possession date, and what stays (appliances, fixtures). *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Respond to inspection requests and complete agreed repairs, with receipts. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Get the mortgage payoff statement requested through the title company. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** **Wire fraud caution:** verify any wiring instructions by phone with a number you already trust. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Book movers and vehicle shipping for dates built around the closing date. Confirm cancellation terms. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Book temporary housing if there's a gap between closing and Oregon move-in. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Keep **homeowner's insurance active** until closing. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Keep **all utilities on** until closing or possession. The buyer's inspection and walkthrough need them. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Start packing non-essentials. Keep staging pieces until the sale is secure. *(MED)*

### PHASE D: Weeks 6-3 before move
- [ ] **J** Schedule utility **final reads and transfers tied to closing**. Call each provider with the closing date. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Notify the HOA and arrange payoff or transfer fees if applicable. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Update address with banks, cards, insurers, payroll, and SSA. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Start USPS forwarding. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Compile **manuals, warranties, and spare keys** into one labeled folder or bin for the buyer. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Clear the **attic and garage** (see checklist in the one-pager). *(HIGH, plan a full weekend or two)*
- [ ] **J** Schedule bulk trash pickup or a junk removal service for leftover items. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Dog tag, route lodging, and dog care for moving day. *(HIGH)*

### PHASE E: Final 2 weeks
- [ ] **J** Confirm closing time, location, and ID needed with the title company. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Confirm mover arrival window, truck access, and payment method. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Pack everything except daily essentials. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Photograph valuables and serial numbers. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Schedule a professional move-out clean if the contract requires broom-clean or better. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Confirm agreed repairs are finished and that receipts are with the realtor. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Collect all keys, remotes, fobs, mailbox keys, and codes. *(HIGH)*

### PHASE F: Moving day and closing
- [ ] **J** Move out fully. Sweep and clean. Leave agreed items in place. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** **Final walkthrough** with the buyer or realtor, usually 24-48 hours before closing. Be ready to answer questions and show repairs. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** **Photograph meter readings** (electric, gas, water) with a timestamp on the day of possession or closing. Send them to the utilities and the realtor. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Leave the manuals folder, garage remotes, and all keys in the agreed spot, or hand them to the realtor. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Attend closing or sign remotely. Review the settlement statement for prorated taxes, HOA, and utilities. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Keep copies of everything signed. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **M** Hit the road with the dog on schedule. *(HIGH)*

### PHASE G: After closing and arrival
- [ ] **J** Confirm funds received and the mortgage is paid off, with written confirmation. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Cancel the Ohio homeowner's insurance after closing, and ask about a refund. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** Keep closing records, improvement receipts, and the settlement statement for taxes. The federal home-sale exclusion may apply, so check with a tax professional. *(MED)*
- [ ] **M** Oregon DMV, vehicle registration, emissions check if applicable, dog license, and vet visit. *(HIGH)*
- [ ] **J** Update voter registration. *(MED)*
- [ ] **J** File part-year resident returns for Ohio and Oregon next tax season. *(MED)*

*(The earlier sections on documents, budget, dog, and services still apply. Seller-specific budget items to add: agent commission, closing costs, repair credits, staging, cleaning, junk removal, and possible double housing costs.)*

# PART 2: PACKING, DECLUTTER, AND ROOM-BY-ROOM

**Packing timeline:** Start with storage/garage/attic (T-8 to T-4), then guest room, decor, books, off-season (T-5 to T-3), living room and bedrooms (T-2), bathrooms (T-1), kitchen last (final week).

**Declutter tips**
- Movers charge by weight or space, so every item cut saves money. Ask whether you'd buy it again today.
- Remove personal photos and thin out closets, since buyers need to picture themselves in the house.
- Sell large items locally. Donate the rest. Skip moving cheap, bulky items.
- Set a hard deadline: everything leaving the house by T-3 weeks.
- Don't move hazmat (propane, paint, fuel, pesticides). Movers won't take it. Dispose of it through county household hazardous waste programs.

**Room-by-room**
- [ ] **Attic:** Empty completely. Sort keep/sell/toss. Check for forgotten items behind insulation areas.
- [ ] **Garage:** Sort tools, seasonal gear, and paint. Sweep. Address oil stains. Collect openers and remotes.
- [ ] **Living room:** Pack decor and media first. Photograph how electronics are wired.
- [ ] **Bedrooms:** Keep a week of clothes out. Use wardrobe boxes or bags for hanging clothes.
- [ ] **Bathrooms:** Pack medications separately and keep them with you. Seal liquids in bags.
- [ ] **Kitchen:** Use paper plates for a few days. Label knives. Pack a "first-night" box.
- [ ] **Office:** Back up computers. Keep laptops, chargers, and important papers with you.
- [ ] **Basement/laundry:** Empty the washer and dryer lines. Check the mover's appliance prep requirements.
- [ ] **Every box:** Label with room and contents. Put heavy items in small boxes.
